items.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: That’s what Lester Young, Prez, used to say. He called everybody “lady” like “Lady Ellis,” he’d say, well we were playing on the stage and if I played particularly well he’d say, “Sing me a song, Lady Ellis.”

ctx.x: That process, I have a term for that process, but I’d like you to expand on it and that is editing as much as creating.

That’s a good way to put it. Well it says it itself you know. But learning what to edit. That’s the secret. Learning. And once you learn to edit like that then your melodies seem to get a lot stronger for some reason. I can tell by the audience reaction if I’m playing really good. And when you’re playing good it’s more melodic. That’s what Lester Young, Prez, used to say.
